story.what_it_does: BLS is a visa and consular services company that runs application centres for governments, and it also has a growing digital services business. In FY26 it earned revenue of ₹2,998 crore, mostly from visa work, while digital grew sharply through the Aadifidelis acquisition.
story.plans: Management targets revenue of ₹6,300 crore by FY30, growth of 20% every year through FY30, and an EBITDA margin of 28% by FY30. Near term it aims to complete the Aadhaar investment (₹75 crore of ₹125 crore done) and start full revenue in Q4 FY27, and to keep the Visa & Consular EBITDA margin near 40%.
story.moat: The notes point to long-term government mandates and contract wins, with self-managed centres helping Visa & Consular margins reach about 40%. The flip side is that the business depends on a small number of large government contracts, and one Punjab agreement was terminated earlier.

scenarios.story: Contract renewals worth $1-2 billion over two years are won, and digital growth plus the Aadhaar project lift revenue toward the ₹6,300 crore FY30 target. Visa margins stay near 40% and net cash keeps building.
signals_to_watch: Visa and Consular EBITDA margin staying around 40% (41.9% in Q2 FY27)
Aadhaar investment completed and full revenue starting by Q4 FY27

scenarios.story: Revenue keeps growing quickly, helped by acquisitions and digital, but the margin mix shifts toward lower-margin digital work. Profit grows more slowly than sales, as seen in Q2 FY27 (revenue up 32%, PAT up 8.6%).
signals_to_watch: Consolidated EBITDA margin versus the 28% FY30 target (25.5% in Q2 FY27)
Digital EBITDA margin (7.4% in Q2 FY27)

scenarios.story: Geopolitical travel disruption and flat visa volumes hold back the core business, while contract concentration adds risk. Lower-margin digital work and acquisition amortisation keep squeezing profit.
signals_to_watch: Visa application volumes, which were flat year on year in Q1 FY27
Visa and consular revenue growth versus the 10-15% guided (11.2% in Q2 FY27)
